steps.message:
The DER Program Office needs the written response to Northline Renewables' pre-application request dated 07/02/2025 on Feeder ALN-108, which asks for written confirmation of available capacity for a 3 MW pure-generation project, before the 08/15/2025 League response. Review 2025-07-02_PreApp_Request_ALN-108.pdf against 2025-07-14_Active_Queue_Report.xlsx and the DER Program records as they stand at 07/14/2025, including the Program Office's own case tracking, and issue the response the Program Office should send, with whatever it has to say about the figure. Record the call on the request's case in the case tracking, log any follow-up the response requires there, and close the case. Return your work as a single Word document, filed in the Program Office's correspondence folder in the document store, giving each determination with the basis you relied on, and the call made one way or the other.

Save it as /filesystem/ALN-108_PreApplication_Response.docx.

Feeder ALN-108 Planning Study — Post-Publication Update Q3 2024
Alleniom Utilities — Distribution Planning
DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com
Doc no. PLN-ALN-108-2024-10 · Rev 1 · Date 10/15/2024 · Owner: Distribution Planning
Prepared by: June Halloway, Distribution Planning Engineer
Contact: june.halloway@alleniom.com
1. Purpose
This memorandum constitutes an interim update to the published Alleniom Utilities Feeder Hosting Capacity Map (HCM-2024-Q2, published 05/15/2024) with respect to Feeder ALN-108 (Elderpine substation, 13.2 kV, pure-generation category). It is issued between scheduled quarterly refreshes of the Hosting Capacity Map to record a material queue addition on the subject feeder that has occurred since the last published map release, so that Distribution Planning staff, applicant-facing correspondence, and pre-application dialogue may be informed of a working interim figure until the next full refresh cycle.
The scope of this document is limited to Feeder ALN-108. It does not modify the published values shown on any other feeder in HCM-2024-Q2, nor does it substitute for a formal feeder-level planning study in support of any specific interconnection application. Applicants and pre-application requesters seeking definitive feeder guidance for project scoping decisions should continue to consult Distribution Planning directly, and any project of consequential size on Feeder ALN-108 will require a full feeder-level planning study following the standard Alleniom Distribution Planning methodology.
2. Baseline: Published Available Capacity
The Alleniom Utilities Feeder Hosting Capacity Map was published on 05/15/2024. The map reflects, on a per-feeder basis, the published available capacity value derived from the most recent completed planning study of record for each feeder as of the publication date, incorporating recorded peak and minimum load, existing interconnected DER of record at the time of the underlying study, and standard thermal, voltage, and protection screens.
For Feeder ALN-108, the published values on HCM-2024-Q2 are as follows:
The 3.0 MW figure shown above is the baseline against which subsequent queue activity is netted for the purposes of this interim update. It remains, until the next scheduled quarterly refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map or an intervening full feeder re-study, the sole published available capacity of record for Feeder ALN-108.
3. Post-Publication Queue Activity
Distribution Planning has reviewed the Active Queue Report as of the date of this document to identify interconnection applications assigned to Feeder ALN-108 that have been queued subsequent to publication of the Hosting Capacity Map. The following post-publication queue entry has been identified on Feeder ALN-108:
The 1.2 MW project queued on 09/18/2024 is a pure-generation interconnection request, consistent with the DER category assigned to the feeder in HCM-2024-Q2. It represents the sole queue addition on Feeder ALN-108 identified in the Active Queue Report between the publication date of the map (05/15/2024) and the date of this study.
No other pending applications, executed interconnection service agreements, or in-service DER additions on Feeder ALN-108 have been identified since publication of HCM-2024-Q2 that would materially alter the baseline figure or the interim netted position stated below.
4. Interim Netted Figure
Applying the post-publication queue entry identified in Section 3 against the published available capacity of record stated in Section 2, the interim netted available capacity figure for Feeder ALN-108 as of the date of this document is calculated as follows:
Interim available capacity: 3.0 MW − 1.2 MW = 1.8 MW.
This interim figure is provided as a working reference for Distribution Planning staff and for use in pre-application correspondence concerning Feeder ALN-108 where such correspondence is issued between quarterly refreshes of the Hosting Capacity Map. The figure is not a substitute for, and does not supersede, the published available capacity value of record on HCM-2024-Q2; the published value remains 3.0 MW until the next map republication.
The interim figure carries the following stated limitations:
It reflects the state of the queue as of the date of this document only. Any subsequent queue additions, withdrawals, or reassignments affecting Feeder ALN-108 that post-date this study are not reflected in the figure above and will require Distribution Planning to reassess the interim position accordingly.
It applies a straight-line nameplate netting against the published available capacity. A full feeder re-study, when performed, may yield a different available capacity value on Feeder ALN-108 depending on updated load recordings, revised existing-DER accounting, and the outcome of thermal, voltage, and protection screens as re-run against current data.
The 1.2 MW queue entry is at the application/queue stage. Should that application be withdrawn or should its final capacity change following study or agreement negotiation, the interim netted figure would require corresponding adjustment.
5. Recommendation
Distribution Planning recommends the following:
Distribution Planning staff should treat 1.8 MW as the working interim available capacity for Feeder ALN-108 in any pre-application dialogue, applicant correspondence, or internal scoping analysis conducted between the date of this document and the next scheduled refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map. The published 3.0 MW figure on HCM-2024-Q2 remains the value of record for the map itself and should not be altered on the published map absent republication.
A refreshed feeder-level planning study for Feeder ALN-108 should be scheduled to be undertaken in advance of, and its results incorporated into, the next full quarterly refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map. Feeder ALN-108 should be included among the feeders prioritized for re-study on the criteria stated in the map front matter: application date of pending queue entries, capacity requested relative to published available headroom, and DER category (pure generation is weighted more heavily against feeder headroom than net-metering behind-the-meter interconnections at equivalent nameplate).
This document should be reissued or superseded if any further queue activity on Feeder ALN-108 arises before the next quarterly map refresh, so that the working interim figure remains accurate as of its date of issue. Distribution Planning will monitor the Active Queue Report accordingly.
Applicants inquiring about Feeder ALN-108 between the date of this document and the next scheduled map republication should be directed to Distribution Planning for confirmation of the interim position before finalizing project sizing decisions, consistent with the general applicability note carried in the front matter of HCM-2024-Q2.

ALLERON MUNICIPAL LEAGUE
812 Larchmont Street · Cordwyn, Alleron 16CW · (651) 555-0244
The united voice of Alleron’s cities, towns, and school districts


Ref: AML-2025-0620-DER
June 20, 2025

Ms. Dana Whitcomb
Vice President, Distribution Operations
Alleniom Utilities
4200 Veldmere Boulevard
Halston, Alleron 01HA

RE: Escalation — DER Interconnection Program Delays Affecting Fourteen Municipalities and School
Districts
Dear Ms. Whitcomb:
On behalf of the Alleron Municipal League and the fourteen member communities identified below, I write to
convey our formal and collective concern regarding the continued and, in our view, unreasonable delays
affecting commercial-scale solar interconnection projects currently stalled within Alleniom Utilities’ Distributed
Energy Resource (DER) interconnection program. This letter follows repeated informal outreach by individual
member staff to your DER Program Office over the preceding several months, outreach which has not produced
the clarity or the timely progress our members need in order to close out their local capital projects.
The League is writing on behalf of 14 municipalities and school districts across the state of Alleron whose
commercial-scale solar projects — commissioned in good faith with voter-approved bond proceeds, adopted
capital budgets, energy-savings performance contracts, and in several instances state and federal grant awards
remain suspended in your interconnection queue awaiting energization. Among the affected members are:
     Brookfen Unified School District
     City of Elmsworth
     Darnwick Community School District
     Lockmere Community School District
     Cravenwood Community School District
     Town of Tresbay
     City of Marden Falls
     Town of Holcott
Additional League members with projects in the same posture have asked to be represented collectively through
this correspondence and are prepared to be identified upon request. Every one of these projects has been
reviewed and approved by the applicable local governing body, financed through public procurement, and
constructed by licensed contractors under permits issued by the relevant authority having jurisdiction.
The projects at issue are not speculative or exploratory. They range in size from approximately 500 kW to nearly
1 MW and are installed at public schools, municipal water and wastewater treatment plants, community centers,
public libraries, and other municipal facilities. In the great majority of cases construction is complete, mechanical
and electrical inspections have been closed out by local inspectors, and equipment has been standing
energized-ready — in some instances for a period now measured in months — pending only the Company’s
authorization to interconnect and place the systems into commercial operation. Each additional month of delay
defers budgeted operating savings, extends the payback horizon presented to our members’ councils and school
boards, and in the case of grant-funded projects places committed public funding at direct risk of forfeiture.
Our members are patient partners. They understand that the interconnection of distributed generation on the
Company’s distribution system requires careful technical review and, at times, coordination with equipment
procurement, feeder studies, and protection-scheme confirmation. They are willing to meet reasonable technical
requirements. What they are not able to accept — and what this League cannot accept on their behalf — is an
 extended period of silence, shifting explanations, and open-ended hold status without a clear articulation of what
is required, by whom, and by when.
Accordingly, and in a spirit of continued cooperation, the League respectfully requests the following from
Alleniom Utilities:
1. A full accounting of current queue status. For each identified League-member project, please provide the
    project’s assigned application number, current queue position, and complete processing history to date.
2. Hold reasons. For every project currently in a hold, pending, or suspended posture, please identify the
    specific reason for the hold, the party responsible for the next action, the information or resource required to
    release the hold, and the date the hold was established.
3. Expected energization dates. For each project, please provide the Company’s current best estimate of the
    date on which Permission to Operate will be issued, together with any intermediate milestone dates
    (studies, equipment delivery, witness testing, or telemetry acceptance) that inform that estimate.
4. A written response. We request the Company’s response in writing, addressed to the undersigned at the
    League’s Cordwyn office, within a reasonable period consistent with the urgency our members’ councils
    and school boards are attaching to this matter.
5. A meeting. We request an in-person meeting between the Company’s senior distribution leadership, the
    League’s executive office, and designated representatives of the affected members, to be scheduled at the
    Company’s offices in Halston or at a mutually convenient location in Cordwyn at the Company’s preference.
    The League is prepared to convene our members on short notice once the Company proposes a date.
For your awareness, a copy of this letter has been provided to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission (APUC),
Energy Resources Division, for the Division’s information. The League has taken this step not as a matter of
confrontation but out of a good-faith obligation to keep the Commission’s staff apprised of a program-level
concern affecting a substantial number of Alleron public entities across multiple service territories within the
Company’s distribution footprint. It remains our strong preference to resolve this matter directly with Alleniom
Utilities.
The League and its members recognize that Alleniom Utilities has been a constructive counterparty on many
prior initiatives, and we approach this escalation with the expectation that the Company shares our interest in
restoring predictable, transparent processing timelines to the DER program. Our members’ communities have
invested public funds, published expected in-service dates to their constituents, and in several cases entered
into contractual arrangements predicated on interconnection occurring by dates that are now past. The credibility
of local government energy planning across Alleron is meaningfully bound up in the outcome, and we are
confident the Company understands the seriousness with which we, our elected officials, and our school boards
regard it.
I would be grateful for the courtesy of an acknowledgment of receipt at your earliest convenience, and I remain
available to discuss any aspect of the foregoing at the telephone number above. Thank you for your prompt
attention to this matter.

Respectfully submitted,


Alden Pryce
Alden Pryce
Executive Director
Alleron Municipal League

Capitol Plaza, Suite 900, Cordwyn, Alleron 14CW

            One Capitol Plaza, Suite 900 · Cordwyn, Alleron 14CW · (651) 555-0180 · apuc.alleron.gov

Halston, Alleron 01HA

Re: APUC Information Request — Alleniom Utilities DER Interconnection Program Backlog
Docket APUC-2025-ER-014

Dear Ms. Ngoyi:

The Energy Resources Division of the Alleron Public Utilities Commission (APUC) is in receipt of
correspondence from the Alleron Municipal League dated 06/20/2025 (AML Ref:
AML-2025-0620-DER), copied to the Division, escalating on behalf of fourteen member municipalities
and school districts a program-level concern with the current pace of commercial-scale Distributed
Energy Resource (DER) interconnection processing on the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The
League's letter identifies delays affecting projects at public schools, municipal water and wastewater
facilities, community centers, and public libraries across multiple communities within the Company's
service territory, and raises questions regarding queue status, hold posture, and expected energization
timelines that fall within the Division's continuing oversight of the Company's APUC-filed
interconnection tariff.

The Division intends to be in a position to brief the Commission on the matter at the previously
scheduled DER program briefing on 09/10/2025. In advance of that briefing, and to permit the Division
to assess the Company's DER interconnection program on the basis of the Company's own records
rather than the League's characterization, this letter requests the following information from Alleniom
Utilities.

1. Commercial DER queue accounting.
For the commercial DER interconnection program (i.e., the ≥500 kW program-scope portfolio
administered by the Company's DER Program Office; simplified small-systems process filings are
outside the scope of this request), the Company is requested to provide a complete queue accounting as
of the most recent full week preceding the response date, including at minimum the following,
presented at the individual-application level and separately summarized in totals:

   a. The count and identity of all applications currently in active processing status, together with each
      application's assigned application number, applicant name, site, nameplate capacity, filing date,
      current processing step, and the study or decision milestone next due.
    b.     The count and identity of all applications currently on on-hold, pending-customer,
        pending-standards, or suspended status, together with the specific hold reason of record for
        each, the party responsible for the next action, the information or resource required to release the
        hold, and the date the hold was established.
   c. The count and identity of all applications for which one or more study or processing timelines
      established under the Company's filed interconnection tariff, procedures, or executed study
      agreements have been exceeded as of the reporting date, together with the timeline of record, the
      actual elapsed time, and the current cause of the overrun.
   d. The count and identity of all applications withdrawn — whether by written applicant request, by
      application of the tariff's deemed-withdrawal provision, or otherwise — during the twelve
      months preceding the reporting date, together with the effective date of each withdrawal and the
      recorded basis for it.
   e.     The count and identity of all formal Notices of Impending Withdrawal, Notices of
        Cancellation, or equivalent written notices issued by the Company to applicants during the
        twelve months preceding the reporting date, together with the notice date, the date sent, the
        method of service, the response deadline computed under the tariff, and the current disposition
        (response received / no response / deemed withdrawn / other).
Where any of the foregoing counts is materially affected by data-integrity items known to the Company
(for example, timing differences, reconciliation items, or other known data-quality issues), the Company is
requested to identify those items and provide the counts both as they presently appear in the Company's
queue records and as the Company understands the underlying facts to be.

2. Backlog-cause summary.
The Company is further requested to provide a written summary describing, in the Company's own
characterization, the principal causes of the current backlog in the commercial DER interconnection
program. The summary should address at a minimum: application volume relative to processing
capacity; the availability and lead time of utility-owned equipment required for energization (including
but not limited to RTU and protection equipment); the status of any internal standards reconciliation
activity affecting screening or protection determinations; the sufficiency of certified-equipment
references relied upon by the Company; the sufficiency of hosting-capacity information made available
to prospective applicants; and any other factors the Company identifies as materially contributing to the
current queue posture. Supporting quantitative material (equipment delivery schedules, staffing
utilization, study cycle times, and the like) is welcome and, where practicable, requested.

3. Format and timing.
Responses should be provided in writing, addressed to the undersigned at the Division's Cordwyn
office, with electronic copies to the docket. Line-item responses under Item 1 above may be provided
by workbook attachment provided each attachment is unambiguously cross-referenced to the
corresponding item. Responses should be received by the Division sufficiently in advance of the
09/10/2025 briefing to allow the Division adequate review; the Division requests that the Company
provide its response no later than 08/22/2025, and, where any portion of the response cannot be
furnished by that date, that the Company so advise the Division in writing no later than 08/08/2025 with
an explanation and a proposed alternative date.

4. Continuing dialogue.
 This request is issued in the ordinary course of the Division's monitoring of interconnection program
performance under the Company's APUC-filed tariff. The Division has no present view as to the merits
of the underlying matter and takes no position on the specific project-level concerns raised in the
League's 06/20/2025 letter, which remain properly a matter between the League's member entities and
the Company in the first instance. The Division's interest at this stage is limited to the queue accounting
and backlog-cause information described above, together with the Company's plan for restoring
predictable processing to the program. The Division remains available to discuss scope, format, or
timing questions at Company request.

The Division appreciates the Company's continued cooperation and looks forward to the Company's
response.

Sincerely,

Nia Fairweather

Alleron Public Utilities Commission

Alleniom Utilities — Regulatory Affairs

INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
TO: DER Program Manager
CC: Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations
Meera Vellanki, Manager, Interconnection Studies
Ivo Grantham, Manager, DER Planning Group
FROM: Harriet Ngoyi, Director, Regulatory Affairs
DATE: 07/01/2025
SUBJECT: DER Backlog Review — Program Manager Tasking
1. Confirmation of directive
This memorandum confirms and operationalizes the internal directive issued 06/27/2025 by Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations (DIR-2025-0627), ordering a full backlog review of the commercial DER interconnection program. Regulatory Affairs accepts ownership of the external commitments arising from that directive and, by this memorandum, assigns the internal queue-cleanup work to the DER Program Manager.
The scope of the backlog review, as established by the VP, is the entire active, on-hold, and past-study-timeline population of the commercial DER program queue as of the anchor date. Every application is to be accounted for by name, application number, current posture, and next required action. Nothing in this memorandum reduces, expands, or alters that scope.
2. Governing deadlines
Two dates fix the outer boundary of this work and are not to be revisited without written concurrence from the VP office and Regulatory Affairs:
08/15/2025 — Response to the Alleron Municipal League. Regulatory Affairs will issue the formal written response to the League's 06/20/2025 letter. The response will be substantive and project-specific, addressing the League's five enumerated requests on behalf of the fourteen member municipalities and school districts. Regulatory Affairs is the signatory; the DER Program Manager is responsible for delivering the underlying queue accounting on which the response will rest.
09/10/2025 — APUC briefing. The queue accounting must be complete and defensible in advance of the briefing to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission's Energy Resources Division. Regulatory Affairs will not present partial data to the Commission. Any application whose disposition remains open on 09/10/2025 must have a written reason on file, not an oral one.
Any interim regulatory information request the Division may issue in advance of the briefing will be answered from the same underlying record and will not create a separate work product for the Program Manager beyond timely disposition of the affected applications.
3. Tasking of the DER Program Manager
The DER Program Manager is tasked, effective immediately, with producing the following queue-cleanup inputs. Each input is to be closed on the record — with the supporting document, tariff citation, standard, or operating guideline named in the file — before it is reported as complete.
3.1 On-hold list dispositions. Work the current on-hold population by hold-reason category. For each project, determine the correct disposition under the applicable tariff provisions and program policy, and clear holds where the underlying reason has resolved. Cross-reference hold-reason categories against the relevant queue and financial records. Business-day counts must follow the standard business-day convention.
3.2 Applications-intake corrections. Review the active queue for duplicate, ghost, and stale-status records. Where a customer has filed a new application at a site with a prior, silently abandoned filing, resolve the intake question in writing before either record is closed or merged. Queue-date assignment must follow the written policy.
3.3 Standards-conflict routing. For every project currently sitting on a standards-clarification hold, determine and execute the correct disposition under applicable program standards and operating procedures.
3.4 Equipment allocation. Convene the equipment-allocation determination for the sites that have completed construction and are awaiting utility-owned equipment. Rank the sites under the applicable equipment deployment prioritization guideline in accordance with its procedures, and match against the current supplier delivery schedule reported by SCADA/EMS Engineering.
3.5 Aggregation determinations. For applications proposing new DER at sites that may host existing generation, apply the applicable aggregation provision before finalizing program-scope routing.
3.6 Capacity verifications. For any application on abnormality hold due to a stated-vs-nameplate capacity discrepancy, verify the nameplate from the application's technical documentation and apply the applicable interconnection standard to any claimed operating limit below inverter nameplate.
3.7 Hosting-capacity corrections. Before any capacity figure from the published hosting-capacity map is communicated externally, confirm that the figure reflects the current state of the affected feeder. A priority refresh is to be requested from Distribution Planning under the published refresh-prioritization criteria.
3.8 Witness-test dispositions. Verify each inverter model against the applicable certified equipment list under the commissioning procedure in effect at the time of determination. Waiver eligibility is to be determined against the applicable certified equipment list.
3.9 Supplemental-review reversals. Review any supplemental-review determination on file for consistency with current program procedures. Where the record requires revision, update the file and flag any prior memorandum that has been superseded accordingly.
4. Reporting cadence
The DER Program Manager will provide weekly progress reports to Regulatory Affairs, with copy to the VP office, every Friday by close of business beginning 07/04/2025 and continuing through 09/12/2025. The weekly report will comprise:
counts by disposition category, aligned to the categories in §3 above;
items closed on the record during the reporting week, with the governing citation named;
exceptions requiring Regulatory Affairs or VP attention, including any project at risk of missing 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025;
forward-look for the following reporting week.
Reports are to be delivered in writing. Verbal updates do not substitute.

 SECTION 12 — INTERCONNECTION OF DISTRIBUTED ENERGY
 RESOURCES
 §12.1 Applicability
 This section governs the interconnection to Alleniom Utilities' (the “Company”) distribution system
 of distributed energy resources (“DER”) within the Alleron service territory. Technical
 requirements, screens, study procedures, and equipment standards referenced herein are set out
 in the Company's DER Interconnection Standard (DIS-01) and companion standards, each of
 which is incorporated by reference. Nothing in this section shall be construed to modify or
 supersede any applicable safety, reliability, or protection requirement of the Company's
 engineering standards.




APUC Tariff Filing — Alleniom Utilities Electric Tariff, Vol. III, §12                     Page 1 of 6
 Alleniom Utilities — APUC-Filed Interconnection Tariff · §12 Interconnection   Volume III · Sheet No. 214




 §12.2 Scope of the DER Interconnection Program
 The DER Interconnection Program administered under this section applies to applications for DER
 interconnection at or above five hundred kilowatts (≥500 kW). Within the Program, DER shall be
 classified according to the DER Interconnection Standard as follows:

     (a) Commercial small-scale DER — five hundred kilowatts to one megawatt (500 kW – 1
        MW);
     (b) Medium-scale DER — one megawatt to five megawatts (1 MW – 5 MW).

 The Program scope threshold is ≥500 kW. DER below five hundred kilowatts (sub-500 kW),
 whether commercial or residential, are not administered under this section and shall instead be
 processed under the Company's Simplified Small-Systems Process, which is filed separately
 and is outside the DER Interconnection Program.

 Aggregation, controlled-capacity recognition, and shared point-of-interconnection eligibility are
 addressed in the DER Interconnection Standard and shall control the classification of any facility
 whose nameplate rating, aggregate site rating, or point of common coupling brings it within
 Program scope.




APUC Tariff Filing — Alleniom Utilities Electric Tariff, Vol. III, §12                       Page 2 of 6
 Alleniom Utilities — APUC-Filed Interconnection Tariff · §12 Interconnection             Volume III · Sheet No. 214




 §12.3 Application Intake and Queue Position
 A complete application shall establish the applicant's queue position as of the date the Company
 determines the application to be complete. Applications determined to be incomplete shall be
 returned with a written deficiency notice identifying each item requiring cure and the date by which
 cure is required. Queue position is not transferable between applications except as expressly
 provided in the DER Interconnection Standard.

 §12.4 Deemed Withdrawal Following Notice of Impending Withdrawal or Cancellation
 Upon issuance of a formal written Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation by the
 Company, the applicant shall have thirty (30) business days from the date of the notice to submit
 a substantive response curing the matter identified therein. If the applicant fails to respond within
 thirty (30) business days, the application shall be deemed withdrawn and shall be closed from the
 active queue without further action of the Company.

 For purposes of this section, “business days” shall exclude Saturdays, Sundays, and federal
 legal public holidays observed within the response window. Without limitation, the following
 federal holidays falling within response windows relevant to the current filing period are recognized
 as non-business days and shall not be counted:

   Holiday                                                               Observed Date

   Memorial Day                                                          05/26/2025

   Juneteenth National Independence Day                                  06/19/2025

   Independence Day                                                      07/04/2025

 The Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation shall be served in writing (certified mail or
 verified electronic delivery) and shall state the date of issuance, the response deadline computed
 under this section, and the consequence of non-response. The Company shall maintain a log of all
 notices issued, dates of service, and dispositions.




APUC Tariff Filing — Alleniom Utilities Electric Tariff, Vol. III, §12                                 Page 3 of 6
 Alleniom Utilities — APUC-Filed Interconnection Tariff · §12 Interconnection   Volume III · Sheet No. 214




 §12.5 Construction-Payment Defaults
 Where a construction work order or interconnection facilities invoice becomes payable and the
 customer has not remitted the amount due, the Company shall inform the customer in writing of
 the outstanding balance and shall issue a payment deadline of thirty (30) business days from
 the date of that written notice.

 For so long as the thirty (30) business-day payment deadline is running, the affected project shall
 remain on hold in the queue and shall NOT be deemed withdrawn. The construction-payment
 default procedure under this §12.5 is distinct from, and shall not be conflated with, the
 deemed-withdrawal procedure under §12.4; the two mechanisms have different triggers, different
 consequences, and different cure paths.

 Upon receipt of full payment prior to expiration of the deadline, the Company shall promptly
 release the hold and resume the affected work in queue order. If the deadline expires without
 payment, the Company may pursue such remedies as are available under the applicable
 Interconnection Service Agreement and this tariff, including, as a separate and subsequent step,
 issuance of a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under §12.4.

Standards Engineering · DER Program

Document control
 Document number                ERP-9
 Revision                       Rev 2
 Effective date                 03/24/2025
 Supersedes                     ERP-9 Rev 1 (07/10/2022)
 Owner                          Alleniom Standards Engineering
 Approved by                    Manager, Standards Engineering
 Distribution                   Alleniom DER Program Office; Interconnection Studies; Distribution Protection
                                Engineering; SCADA/EMS Engineering; DER Planning Group; Regulatory
                                Affairs
 Attachments                    Bulletin EB-2025-03 (03/24/2025); Form ER-11 template; Precedent Register



Revision history
 Rev         Date            Summary
 Rev 1       07/10/2022      Initial issue. Established referral form and per-site engineering determination path.
 Rev 2       03/24/2025      Reissued in conjunction with Bulletin EB-2025-03. §3 rewritten to state routing rule
                             for standards conflicts; Form ER-11 fields expanded to capture site type and feeder;
                             precedent register appended.



§1 PURPOSE
ERP-9 establishes the procedure by which an interconnection application encountering a standards
conflict, a silence between standards, or site conditions falling outside the assumptions of a tabulated
requirement is referred to a per-site protection/SCADA engineering determination. The procedure exists so
that documentary conflicts between Alleniom standards do not accumulate as screening holds against
active applications, and so that each affected site is resolved on the merits of its own protection scheme,
on a schedule stated in §4.

This procedure is issued by Standards Engineering and applies uniformly across the Alleniom DER
Program. It is read together with DIS-01 (DER Interconnection Standard), DPS-07 (Distribution Protection
Standard), TCS-02 (Telemetry & Communications Standard), and the APUC-filed interconnection tariff.
 §2 SCOPE
ERP-9 applies to any in-scope DER application administered by the Alleniom DER Program at which one
or more of the following conditions is encountered during initial screening, supplemental review, or system
impact study:

    (1) Two applicable Alleniom standards state requirements that cannot both be applied on their face to
    the affected site.
    (2) An applicable standard is silent as to a site condition materially present in the application (a topic
    on which the standard does not speak, as distinct from a topic on which it speaks and permits an
    exception).
    (3) The reviewing engineer documents a reasoned basis to depart from a tabulated requirement in
    light of the site's specific protection arrangement.
Sub-scope facilities handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application
of ERP-9; the Small-Systems reviewer may nonetheless invoke Form ER-11 where an export configuration
warrants site-specific protection engineering input.

Nothing in this procedure permits a screening hold pending revision of a standard where ERP-9 provides a
determination path. See §3 and Bulletin EB-2025-03 (attached).

§3 REFERRAL ROUTING
Any standards conflict encountered at screening or design shall be routed via Form ER-11 to a per-site
protection/SCADA engineering determination. No “winning” document is selected across the program;
each site is resolved on its own protection scheme.

The reviewing engineer in Interconnection Studies initiates the referral by completing Form ER-11
(template attached), attaching the relevant excerpts of the standards at issue, the application's connection
diagram and equipment schedule, and any feeder-specific information required to characterize the site's
protection arrangement. Interconnection Studies transmits the completed Form ER-11 to Distribution
Protection Engineering; where SCADA/EMS input is required, the Manager, Distribution Protection
Engineering routes a copy to the SCADA/EMS Engineering group for concurrent review.

Referral does not itself alter the application's status in the DER Program queue. The affected application
remains in queue during the referral period, and other screening activities that are not dependent on the
referred question shall proceed in parallel.

The per-site engineering determination is issued in writing on Form ER-11 by Distribution Protection
Engineering, is signed by the responsible engineer and countersigned by the Manager, Distribution
Protection Engineering, and is filed with the application record. The determination is binding for the
referred site and does not create a general rule across the program; a subsequent site presenting a similar
question is referred and determined on its own facts.

Where the site's protection arrangement, as determined under this section, differs from the tabular default
of DIS-01 §5 Table 5-1, the engineering determination on Form ER-11 supplements the site's
protective-equipment scoping and is provided to the DER Program Office and to the contracts desk for
incorporation into the interconnection service agreement.

Where the referral resolves a recurring pattern that Standards Engineering considers appropriate to reflect
in a future revision of a standard, the determinations are logged and reviewed as provided in §5.
 §4 TIMELINES
Timelines below run from the date on which Interconnection Studies transmits the completed Form ER-11
to Distribution Protection Engineering. Business days exclude weekends and federal holidays.

 Referral class                     Description                                                Determination due
 Class A — Standards conflict,      Two Alleniom standards state conflicting requirements at   10 business days
 no site protection novelty         a site whose protection arrangement is otherwise
                                    ordinary.
 Class B — Standards conflict       Conflict at a site whose arrangement (e.g.,                20 business days
 with site protection novelty       load/generation decoupling, non-standard grounding,
                                    unusual feeder configuration) requires additional
                                    protection engineering review.
 Class C — Standards silence,       Applicable standard is silent as to a site condition       30 business days
 site condition outside tabulated   materially present. Determination may require
 assumptions                        coordination study.
 Class D — SCADA/EMS input          Any of the above where the site's telemetry or control     30 business days
 required in addition to            arrangement requires concurrent SCADA/EMS
 protection engineering             Engineering review.

Classification is made by the Manager, Distribution Protection Engineering, on receipt of Form ER-11.
Where the reviewer requests reclassification, the request is decided in writing within two business days.

Extensions to the timelines above are permitted only in writing, are issued by the Manager, Distribution
Protection Engineering, and are copied to the DER Program Manager and Regulatory Affairs. Applications
shall not be held in queue pending revision of a standard where this procedure provides a determination
path; extensions do not authorize a screening hold outside this procedure.

 ALLENIOM UTILITIES — DISTRIBUTION OPERATIONS

 EQUIPMENT DEPLOYMENT PRIORITIZATION
 GUIDELINE
 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA

 Doc no.                    Rev              Effective Date        Owner

 OG-17                      Rev 1            04/07/2025            Alleniom Distribution
                                                                   Operations



 Document Control
 Supersedes: none (initial issue).
 Review cycle: annual, or on material change to supplier lead times or operating criticality categories.
 Approving authority: VP, Distribution Operations.
 Distribution: DER Program Office; Interconnection Studies; DER Planning Group; System Operations Center
 (SOC); Standards Engineering; Supply Chain — Distribution Equipment.

 §1 SCOPE
 This guideline governs deployment sequencing of constrained utility equipment (RTUs, reclosers) across
 completed sites awaiting energization. It applies to Alleniom-owned devices installed by Distribution
 Operations for the purpose of energizing a construction-complete distributed energy resource (DER) site,
 when supplier lead times or quarterly delivery quantities constrain the number of sites that can be
 equipped in a given deployment window.

 This guideline does NOT apply to application processing. Nondiscriminatory queue-order treatment of
 interconnection applications is governed by Interconnection Tariff §12.7 and by the procedures
 administered by Interconnection Studies; nothing in this guideline modifies, displaces, or supplements
 those procedures. The rankings established under §2 operate solely on sites for which interconnection
 application processing is complete, the interconnection agreement (where required) is executed, and
 construction is certified complete by the customer or its contractor.

 Devices out of scope: customer-owned protective equipment; utility-owned equipment already installed at
 the site; distribution-system reinforcement equipment scheduled under an approved capital work order.
 Program scope for the underlying DER remains as defined in DIS-01 Rev 4 §3 and Interconnection Tariff
 §12.2.

 §2 COMMISSIONING CRITICALITY
 As a general rule, deployment priority for constrained equipment follows interconnection queue order,
 consistent with the nondiscriminatory treatment principles of Interconnection Tariff §12.7.
 A site may be advanced ahead of queue order under certain circumstances — the urgent nature of a
 request, in particular for public infrastructure (schools, hospitals, water/wastewater facilities), or an
 expedited deployment pathway on reasonable customer request — but only where substantiated by the
 site's own recorded attributes (per §3), in order of priority: (1) essential-service function (water/wastewater,
 emergency, health); (2) committed in-service or grant-funding deadline; (3) construction-complete date.
 Among sites of the same critical nature, the deciding factor is interconnection queue order; requests not
 substantiated by these attributes remain in queue order.

OG-17 Rev 1 — Equipment Deployment Prioritization Guideline                                                 Page 1
  Factor definitions:

   •   Essential-service function. A site whose primary served load is a public water or wastewater facility;
       a hospital, emergency-response, or first-responder facility; or a public-health facility for which loss of
       service is treated as an emergency by the responsible jurisdiction. Essential-service status is
       evidenced by the customer's facility classification of record and, where applicable, the served-load
       designation on the interconnection application.
   •   Committed in-service or grant-funding deadline. A contractually committed in-service date, or a
       date on which grant funding lapses if the site is not in service, established in a fully executed written
       instrument between the customer and a governmental funder, project sponsor, or off-taker. Internal
       customer construction targets, marketing dates, budget-cycle expectations, and school-year,
       fiscal-year, or seasonal preferences do not constitute a committed deadline under this factor.
   •   Construction-complete date. The calendar date on which the customer's construction of the site
       was certified complete and ready for utility energization steps. Where more than one date is recorded,
       the earlier of (a) the customer's written notice of construction completion and (b) the utility's on-site
       verification, controls.
   •   Queue date as tiebreaker. The interconnection queue date of the site's underlying application, used
       only to break a tie among sites that rank equally on factors (1), (2), and (3).
 External advocacy, correspondence volume, elected-official inquiries, and stakeholder communications
 received in relation to a site do not enter the ranking. Ranking is determined from the raw attributes above,
 evidenced by the source documents in §3.

 §3 DOCUMENTATION
 For each deployment window the DER Program Office shall assemble a deployment worksheet listing
 every site meeting the eligibility conditions of §1, with the following fields drawn from the identified system
 of record:

   •   Site name and interconnection application ID (DER Program queue).
   •   Customer / party of record and site service address (DER Program queue).
   •   Nameplate capacity and program-scope classification per DIS-01 Rev 4 §3 (application file).
   •   Devices required to energize (RTU, POI recloser, or both), quantities, and specification references
       (Standards Engineering).
   •   Construction-complete date and source of certification (project construction file).
   •   Contracted in-service or grant-funding deadline, if any, with the executed instrument establishing it
       attached by reference (customer submission).
   •   Essential-service classification, if any, with the customer's facility classification of record attached b

      • eligibility to share an existing point of interconnection where legacy equipment is on site (§3.5);
      • recognition of a controlled operating limit below nameplate (§3.6);

 are established under TCS-02 and are not restated here except by cross-reference.

 §3.1 Determination of aggregate nameplate capacity
 Aggregate nameplate capacity is the sum of the manufacturer-rated ac output ratings of all generating equipment
 interconnected, or proposed to be interconnected, at a single point of common coupling. Manufacturer datasheets
 govern; derated or "operating" figures do not substitute for nameplate except as provided in §3.6.

 §3.2 Point of common coupling
 The point of common coupling is the point at which the DER facility is electrically connected to the Company's
 distribution system, as further defined in IEEE 1547-2018. The PCC is distinct from the point of interconnection (POI),
 the latter being the physical demarcation of Company-owned protective and metering equipment.

 §3.3 Determination on the basis of application
 Classification is determined on the facility as filed and as physically configured on site. Filing captions, project titles,
 and cover-letter characterizations do not alter classification; the connection diagram, the equipment schedule, and
 the address of record govern.

 §3.4 Aggregation
 Co-located DER behind the same point of common coupling counts toward one site total.

 Previously interconnected legacy equipment counts toward the aggregate regardless of the vintage of its permission
 to operate, regardless of whether it predates any current Alleniom standard, and regardless of the sequence or form
 in which subsequent applications are submitted at the same PCC. The aggregate governs the facility class and the
 resulting program-scope determination.

 An applicant proposing a new DER at a premises that already hosts DER shall identify the existing equipment on the
 application form and shall submit a one-line diagram showing the electrical relationship of the proposed equipment,
 the existing equipment, the customer load, the customer meter, and the PCC. Interconnection Studies verifies against
 the Company existing-DER register.

 §3.5 Shared-POI eligibility
 A new DER may share an existing POI only where the combined facility, including legacy equipment, can be brought
 to current monitoring/control standards; otherwise a separate POI and a new application are required. Where the
 existing system operates behind the meter, a new DER may instead be interconnected front-of-the-meter under its
 own service and POI, and is then evaluated on its own capacity without aggregation.

 The two dispositions available under §3.5 are:

   1. Shared POI, aggregated. The combined facility (legacy equipment plus proposed equipment) is brought to
      current monitoring/control standards as prescribed by TCS-02 and by Table 5-1 at the aggregate class. The
      applicant is responsible for the retrofit and for demonstrating retrofit feasibility to Interconnection Studies. Where
      feasibility is confirmed, the application proceeds at the aggregate capacity at the shared POI.
   2. Separate POI, non-aggregated front-of-the-meter alternative. Where the existing system operates behind
      the meter and the applicant elects to interconnect the new DER front-of-the-meter under a separate service and
      its own POI, the new DER is evaluated on its own capacity, without aggregation with the legacy equipment.
      Class placement, review path, and Table 5-1 category are determined from the new DER's capacity alone.
 Retrofit feasibility of legacy equipment is a factual question the Company will not decide from records alone; the
 applicant or its authorized developer must confirm feasibility in writing. Absent that confirmation, the shared-POI path
 under §3.5(1) is not available and the application is redirected to §3.5(2) or withdrawn.

 §3.6 Controlled-capacity recognition
 A limit below nameplate is recognized only with a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification plus an approved Control
 Narrative — sufficient in themselves for recognition. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
 recognized limit is enforced as applicable: telemetry monitoring, and on pure-generation sites the POI recloser's ANSI
 32 directional-power element set to the recognized limit and tripping on violation.

 Required submissions. To have a controlled operating limit recognized in place of aggregate nameplate for
 program-scope and study purposes, the applicant shall submit both of the following:

   1. A valid Power Control System (PCS) certification issued under UL 1741 (including Supplement SB where
      applicable) and/or UL 3141, identifying the specific equipment arrangement at the applicant's site and the
      setpoint range.
   2. An approved Control Narrative — a written engineering document describing how the site's control system
      enforces the requested operating limit, including the sensed quantities, the response actions, the response
      times, the interlocks, and any allowable modes and their setpoint ceilings.
 These two documents, taken together, are sufficient in themselves to establish recognition of the controlled limit.
 Recognition establishes the capacity at which the facility is reviewed, classified, and studied.

 Enforcement backstops as arrangement provides. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
 recognized limit is enforced by the arrangement's existing equipment as follows:

      • Telemetry monitoring. For sites at or above the TCS-02 threshold, the Company's RTU-to-SCADA telemetry
      monitors real-power export at the point of interconnection against the recognized limit. Sustained deviation
      triggers investigation under TCS-02 and may result in a hold on permission to operate.
      • POI recloser directional-power element (pure-generation sites). On pure-generation sites — sites at which
      no customer load is served behind the point of common coupling — where a utility POI recloser is installed per
      Table 5-1 and DPS-07, the recloser's ANSI 32 directional-power element is set to the recognized limit and trips
      the site on violation. The ANSI 32 element is inherently available in modern reclosers and does not require
      additional utility hardware.
 Enforcement provisions apply only as the site's arrangement provides them. Their absence at a particular site does
 not reopen the recognition determination once the two required submissions are on file.

 No controlled limit without submissions. In the absence of both a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification and
 an approved Control Narrative, nameplate governs for classification, program-scope determination, and study.

 Certified Equipment List. CEL-2025-Q2 restates this section in its front matter. Listing of a PCS on the current CEL

ALLENION UTILITIES — DER PROGRAM OFFICE
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  (612) 555-0100  ·  der.program@alleniom.com  ·  alleniom.com
PRE-APPLICATION CAPACITY RESPONSE — FEEDER ALN-108 (ELDERPINE)
Response to the Northline Renewables LLC pre-application request dated 07/02/2025; DER Program records reviewed as of 07/14/2025. Issued in advance of the 08/15/2025 written response to the Alleron Municipal League.
[Heading 1] 1.  Purpose and summary of the call
This document is the DER Program Office’s written response to the pre-application request for feeder-capacity confirmation submitted by Northline Renewables LLC on 07/02/2025 for a 3 MW (AC nameplate) pure-generation photovoltaic project on Feeder ALN-108 (Elderpine substation, 13.2 kV). It records each determination with the basis relied on, sets out the written response to be sent to the requester, and records the call on the request’s case in the Program Office case tracking, with the follow-up the response requires, and closes the case. It is issued before the 08/15/2025 written response to the Alleron Municipal League so that any capacity figure communicated externally for Feeder ALN-108 reflects the current state of the feeder.
Summary of the call.  The 3.0 MW published available-capacity figure for Feeder ALN-108 (HCM-2024-Q2, published 05/15/2024) does NOT remain current as of 07/14/2025. Two pure-generation queue entries have been added to Feeder ALN-108 since that publication — Grantwyck Solar LLC (PXA-2024-0231, 1.2 MW, queued 09/18/2024) and Cindermere Renewables LLC (PXA-2025-0044, 1.0 MW, queued 02/06/2025) — totaling 2.2 MW. Adjusted against the published 3.0 MW, the interim available capacity on Feeder ALN-108 is 0.8 MW. The Program Office therefore cannot confirm 3.0 MW of available capacity for a 3 MW pure-generation project; the requested 3 MW exceeds the current available headroom by 2.2 MW.
[Heading 1] 2.  Records reviewed (as of 07/14/2025)
Northline Renewables LLC, Pre-Application Request — 3 MW project on Feeder ALN-108, dated 07/02/2025 (Peter Ashford, Director of Project Development).
Alleniom Utilities Feeder Hosting Capacity Map, HCM-2024-Q2, published 05/15/2024 (Distribution Planning; owner June Halloway) — Title Block and Feeder Capacity tabs, including the Applicability note and the DER-category legend. ALN-108 shown as 3.0 MW, Pure Generation, 13.2 kV, last study 04/2024.
Feeder ALN-108 Planning Study — Post-Publication Update Q3 2024, PLN-ALN-108-2024-10 Rev 1, dated 10/15/2024 (Distribution Planning; June Halloway): interim figure 1.8 MW = 3.0 − 1.2 (Grantwyck), with reissue-on-further-activity and re-study recommendations.
Weekly Active Queue Export, as of 07/14/2025 (DER Program Office) — ALN-108 rows (four active entries).
Weekly On-Hold Queue Export (07/14/2025), Withdrawal Notice Log (07/14/2025), and Existing-DER Register Extract (Screening) — reviewed for any additional ALN-108 holds, withdrawals, or in-service DER additions; none identified that alter the figure.
DER Program Office case tracking / queue-management system, per Queue Management & Withdrawal Policy POL-QM-05 Rev 3 (03/15/2025).
Governing provisions: APUC-filed Interconnection Tariff §12 (Vol. III, Sheet 214, eff. 03/01/2024); DIS-01 Rev 4 (DER Interconnection Standard, eff. 03/01/2024); SRP-3 Rev 3 (Supplemental Review Procedure); POL-QM-05 Rev 3; Regulatory Affairs Tasking Memo RA-2025-07-01 (§3.7 hosting-capacity corrections); Backlog Review Directive DIR-2025-0627.
[Heading 1] 3.  The request
Northline asks the DER Program Office for: (1) written confirmation that the 3.0 MW published availability on Feeder ALN-108 “remains current as of the date of this request,” for a 3 MW (AC) pure-generation interconnection; (2) any known conditions, restrictions, or upgrade indications for a 3 MW project at this location; and (3) scheduling of a pre-application dialogue meeting with Distribution Planning and the DER Program Office. Northline states it scoped the project to 3.0 MW nameplate AC “to sit at, rather than above, the published available figure” and cites HCM-2024-Q2 (05/15/2024), on which ALN-108 shows 3.0 MW available (pure-generation, 13.2 kV, last planning study 04/2024). The request is an inquiry; it is not a filed application and does not establish a queue position (Tariff §12.3).
[Heading 1] 4.  Determinations (basis and call)
Each determination below states the basis relied on and the call made one way or the other.
[Heading 2] Determination 1 — Does the 3.0 MW published available capacity remain current as of 07/14/2025?
Call: NO — it does not remain current.
Basis. HCM-2024-Q2 shows 3.0 MW published available capacity for ALN-108 as of the 05/15/2024 publication date (Feeder Capacity tab: ALN-108, Elderpine, 13.2 kV, 3.0 MW, Pure Generation, last study 04/2024). The HCM Applicability note expressly states that “[p]ublished values do not reflect interconnection queue activity recorded after the publication date; the active-queue register maintained by the DER Program Office is the record of that activity. A pre-application capacity response is prepared against the published value as adjusted for queue entries added since publication.” The 07/14/2025 Active Queue Report shows that two queue entries have been added to Feeder ALN-108 since the 05/15/2024 publication (see Determination 2), so the published 3.0 MW does not reflect the current state of the feeder and is not the figure to be communicated externally. This is reinforced by Regulatory Affairs Tasking Memo RA-2025-07-01 §3.7 (hosting-capacity corrections: before any capacity figure from the published hosting-capacity map is communicated externally, confirm that the figure reflects the current state of the affected feeder, and request a priority refresh from Distribution Planning under the published refresh-prioritization criteria).
[Heading 2] Determination 2 — What is the current available capacity on Feeder ALN-108 as of 07/14/2025?
Call: 0.8 MW interim available capacity (straight-line nameplate netting of post-publication queue additions against the published 3.0 MW).
Basis. The Active Queue Report as of 07/14/2025 lists four active queue entries on Feeder ALN-108:
The two pre-publication entries (Ravenford, queued 2023-11-20; Fenwyn, queued 2024-04-03) were on the queue before the 05/15/2024 publication and are incorporated in the published 3.0 MW baseline (consistent with the 10/15/2024 planning study, which identified Grantwyck as the sole post-publication addition then on record and netted only it). The two post-publication entries (Grantwyck, 1.2 MW, queued 09/18/2024; Cindermere, 1.0 MW, queued 02/06/2025) are netted against the published figure. Both are pure-generation interconnections on a pure-generation feeder, consistent with the feeder’s published DER category; SRP-3 Rev 3 §5(c) and the HCM Applicability note both confirm that queue entries not yet reflected in the published map remain applicable to capacity. Interim available capacity = 3.0 MW − 1.2 MW − 1.0 MW = 0.8 MW. The 10/15/2024 planning study had set the interim figure at 1.8 MW (= 3.0 − 1.2); the 02/06/2025 Cindermere entry is the further queue activity that study anticipated and that reduces the interim figure to 0.8 MW. The On-Hold Queue Report, the Withdrawal Notice Log, and the Existing-DER Register Extract were reviewed; no ALN-108 hold, withdrawal, or in-service DER addition appears that would further change the figure. The 0.8 MW figure is interim, pending a full feeder re-study, and is not a substitute for the published 3.0 MW value of record on the map, which remains 3.0 MW until republication.
[Heading 2] Determination 3 — Can the Program Office confirm 3.0 MW (a 3 MW project) for Northline?
Call: NO. The requested 3 MW (AC nameplate) exceeds the current available headroom.
Basis. Current interim available capacity is 0.8 MW (Determination 2). A 3 MW-AC pure-generation project exceeds the available headroom by 2.2 MW (3.0 − 0.8). It also exceeds the prior 10/15/2024 interim figure of 1.8 MW by 1.2 MW. The Program Office therefore cannot give the written confirmation Northline requests at 3 MW. The AC nameplate governs for interconnection capacity (DIS-01 §3.1; the request states 3 MW-AC, ~3.9 MW-DC). The pre-application request is an inquiry and does not itself establish a queue position or consume feeder capacity (Tariff §12.3), so it is not netted into the figure and creates no double-count.
[Heading 2] Determination 4 — Known conditions, restrictions, or upgrade indications for a 3 MW project here?
Call: A 3 MW project cannot be confirmed on the interim record; it would require a full feeder-level re-study (system impact study) and would likely require distribution-system upgrades and coordinated/cluster study treatment with the queued Grantwyck and Cindermere projects.
Basis. The 0.8 MW interim figure is a straight-line nameplate netting only (per the 10/15/2024 planning study §4); a full feeder re-study may yield a different value once updated load, existing-DER accounting, and thermal/voltage/protection screens are re-run. A 3 MW-AC facility is medium-scale (DIS-01 §3, Table 3-1, 1–5 MW; Category 3), requiring initial screening plus a system impact study (Table 3-1) and a dedicated protection relay, a utility-owned POI recloser, and utility RTU/SCADA telemetry (Table 5-1; TCS-02 §5; DPS-07). Because the requested 3 MW exceeds the interim available headroom, the study would assess what, if any, feeder reinforcement or upgrades are required, and may require cluster treatment with the queued Grantwyck (1.2 MW) and Cindermere (1.0 MW) projects. The 10/15/2024 planning study §5 recommended a refreshed feeder-level re-study for ALN-108 ahead of the next quarterly HCM refresh and that the working interim figure be reissued whenever further queue activity arises — which it now has (Cindermere).
[Heading 2] Determination 5 — Re-sizing options to fit within available headroom
Call: If Northline wishes to proceed before the full re-study, the project would need to be sized to no more than the 0.8 MW interim available headroom (and ultimately to whatever the full re-study supports), with the AC nameplate governing.
Basis. DIS-01 §3.1 (aggregate nameplate = sum of manufacturer-rated AC output ratings; nameplate governs). A controlled operating limit below nameplate may be recognized under DIS-01 §3.6 only with a valid UL 1741/3141 PCS certification plus an approved Control Narrative; listing of a PCS on the Certified Equipment List (CEL-2025-Q2) is not by itself recognition. Northline is best positioned to make this sizing decision after the pre-application dialogue with Distribution Planning and after the re-study.
[Heading 2] Determination 6 — Pre-application dialogue meeting
Call: YES — schedule. The Program Office will convene a pre-application dialogue meeting with Northline and Distribution Planning at Alleniom’s earliest convenience.
Basis. HCM Applicability note (applicants and pre-application requesters should consult Distribution Planning for confirmation before finalizing project sizing); 10/15/2024 planning study §5 (applicants inquiring about ALN-108 between map republications should be directed to Distribution Planning for confirmation of the interim position); request item 3. The meeting will be coordinated with June Halloway, Distribution Planning Engineer.
[Heading 1] 5.  Written response to be sent to Northline Renewables LLC
The letter below is the response the DER Program Office should send to Mr. Ashford. It is ready for issuance on Alleniom Utilities letterhead via der.program@alleniom.com.
Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  der.program@alleniom.com  ·  (612) 555-0100
Date:  July 14, 2025
To:  Peter Ashford, Director of Project Development, Northline Renewables LLC (peter.ashford@northlinerenewables.com)
From:  DER Program Office, Alleniom Utilities
Re:  Pre-Application Request — 3 MW Pure-Generation Project on Feeder ALN-108 (Elderpine Substation Service Area) — Capacity Confirmation
Dear Mr. Ashford:
Thank you for your pre-application request dated July 2, 2025, asking the DER Program Office to confirm the available capacity on Feeder ALN-108 for a 3 MW (AC nameplate) pure-generation photovoltaic project, and for your transparency in sizing the project to the published figure. We have reviewed your request against the Alleniom Utilities Feeder Hosting Capacity Map (HCM-2024-Q2, published 05/15/2024) and the DER Program records as of July 14, 2025, including the active interconnection queue. Our response follows, addressed to each of the three items in your request.
1.  Available capacity on Feeder ALN-108. The 3.0 MW figure shown for Feeder ALN-108 on HCM-2024-Q2 is the published available capacity of record as of the May 15, 2024 publication date. It does not, however, remain current as of the date of your request. As the map’s applicability note states, published values do not reflect interconnection queue activity recorded after the publication date, and a pre-application capacity response is prepared against the published value as adjusted for queue entries added since publication. Since that publication, two pure-generation interconnection applications have been added to the Feeder ALN-108 queue:
Grantwyck Solar LLC (PXA-2024-0231) — 1.2 MW, queued September 18, 2024, currently in system impact study; and
Cindermere Renewables LLC (PXA-2025-0044) — 1.0 MW, queued February 6, 2025, currently in technical screening.
Adjusted against the published 3.0 MW, these two post-publication entries (2.2 MW in total) reduce the interim available capacity on Feeder ALN-108 to 0.8 MW as of July 14, 2025. (Our interim planning study of October 15, 2024 had set the figure at 1.8 MW after the first of these additions; the February 2025 entry is the further queue activity that study anticipated and that brings the interim figure to 0.8 MW.) The published 3.0 MW remains the value of record on the map itself until the next quarterly republication; it is not, however, the figure on which a new project should be sized today.
2.  Confirmation at 3 MW and applicable conditions. On that basis, we are not able to confirm 3.0 MW of available capacity for a 3 MW pure-generation interconnection on Feeder ALN-108. A 3 MW (AC) project exceeds the current interim available headroom of 0.8 MW by 2.2 MW. A 3 MW-AC facility is medium-scale under our DER Interconnection Standard (DIS-01 Rev 4), and a formal application at that size would proceed through initial technical screening and a system impact study, with a dedicated protection relay, a utility-owned point-of-interconnection recloser, and utility RTU/SCADA telemetry required. Because the requested capacity exceeds the interim headroom, the study would determine what feeder reinforcement or upgrades, if any, are required, and may require coordinated (cluster) study treatment with the queued Grantwyck and Cindermere projects. The 0.8 MW figure is an interim, straight-line netting; a full feeder re-study may yield a different value once updated load, existing-DER accounting, and thermal, voltage, and protection screens are re-run.
3.  Sizing options and next steps. If you wish to move forward in advance of the full re-study, the project would need to be sized to no more than the 0.8 MW interim available headroom (the AC nameplate governs for interconnection capacity). A controlled operating limit below nameplate can be recognized under DIS-01 §3.6 with a valid UL 1741/3141 Power Control System certification and an approved Control Narrative; listing on our Certified Equipment List alone is not sufficient for that recognition. We are, in parallel, requesting Distribution Planning to reissue the interim ALN-108 planning study to reflect the February 2025 queue addition and the updated 0.8 MW figure, and to schedule a full feeder-level re-study for ALN-108 ahead of the next quarterly Hosting Capacity Map refresh, so that a definitive figure is available before you finalize sizing.
Pre-application dialogue meeting. As you requested, we will schedule a pre-application dialogue meeting with Northline, the DER Program Office, and Distribution Planning (June Halloway, Distribution Planning Engineer) at Alleniom’s earliest convenience. Our office will be in touch shortly to propose dates. In the meantime, please direct any project-sizing decisions for Feeder ALN-108 to Distribution Planning through this office, consistent with the applicability note carried in the Hosting Capacity Map.
Please note that this pre-application request is an inquiry and does not establish a queue position or reserve feeder capacity; a queue position would be established only on our determination that a complete formal application has been received (Interconnection Tariff §12.3). We welcome the opportunity to work with Northline as you refine the Elderpine Solar I sizing, and we appreciate your having sized to the published figure and flagged the request for confirmation before filing.
Respectfully,
DER Program Office
Alleniom Utilities

def heading(text, level=1):
    h = doc.add_heading(text, level=level)
    for run in h.runs:
        run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x1F, 0x3A, 0x5F)
    return h

def para(text='', bold=False, italic=False, size=None, align=None, space_after=6):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    r = p.add_run(text)
    r.bold = bold
    r.italic = italic
    if size:
        r.font.size = Pt(size)
    if align is not None:
        p.alignment = align
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
    return p

def bullet(text, level=0):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(text, style='List Bullet')
    if level:
        p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.5 + 0.25*level)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
    return p

def kv_table(rows, widths=(1.6, 4.4)):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=0, cols=2)
    t.style = 'Light Grid Accent 1'
    t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.LEFT
    for k, v in rows:
        cells = t.add_row().cells
        cells[0].text = k

        for c in cells:

        cells[0].paragraphs[0].runs[0].bold = True
    for row in t.rows:

Both deliverables are on disk, byte-identical, valid, and render to an 11-page letter-size document.

## Summary

**Deliverable — single Word document, at the exact path the instruction names, plus a copy filed in the Program Office's correspondence folder:**
- `/filesystem/ALN-108_PreApplication_Response.docx` (exact save path)
- `/filesystem/Correspondence/ALN-108_PreApplication_Response.docx` (filed in the Program Office's correspondence folder)

**Final state:** Both files exist, open as valid OOXML (81 paragraphs, 6 tables), are byte-identical (md5 `7504c190…`), and render correctly via LibreOffice to an 11-page letter-size PDF with a footer carrying the doc number and "Page X of 11". All completeness checks pass.

**The call recorded:** The 3.0 MW published figure (HCM-2024-Q2, 05/15/2024) does **not** remain current as of 07/14/2025. Two pure-generation queue entries were added to Feeder ALN-108 after publication — Grantwyck Solar (PXA-2024-0231, 1.2 MW, 09/18/2024) and Cindermere Renewables (PXA-2025-0044, 1.0 MW, 02/06/2025), 2.2 MW total — so interim available capacity = 3.0 − 1.2 − 1.0 = **0.8 MW**. The Program Office **declines to confirm 3.0 MW** (the 3 MW request exceeds headroom by 2.2 MW), advises re-sizing to ≤0.8 MW or awaiting the full feeder re-study, schedules the pre-application dialogue, records the disposition on the case (status CLOSED, 07/14/2025), and logs follow-up items FU-1–FU-4 (Distribution Planning re-study; dialogue meeting; carry the corrected 0.8 MW figure into the 08/15/2025 League response and 09/10/2025 APUC briefing; intake handling).

The document gives each of six determinations with its **Call** (one way or the other) and the **Basis** relied on, followed by the ready-to-send response letter to Northline, the case-tracking record (with the Program Office's own case tracking referenced), and sign-off/distribution.
